items.title: Australian brand has a 'Trump account' after six-figure tariff refund
items.description: Businesses globally are clawing back tens of billions of dollars paid to United States customs after Donald Trump's so-called liberation day tariffs were deemed unlawful.

items.title: Australia's only manganese smelter to close immediately
items.description: The Liberty Bell Bay manganese smelter in northern Tasmania will close immediately after administrators failed to find a buyer for the former GFG Alliance asset.

items.title: Q-Day is coming and it might break the entire internet
items.description: The countdown is on to Q-Day, when an algorithm written more than 30 years ago could run on a quantum computer and compromise the security of data on the internet. How are we preparing?

items.title: England's hopes fade again, but it never stop them dreaming
items.description: England aren't going to be bringing the World Cup home, 60 years of hurt due to extend at least another four years after the devastation of another semifinal defeat. But it won't stop them dreaming.

items.title: Albanese rolls out rule book and red carpet for AI companies
items.description: If Australia is truly going to coax major AI companies to choose us rather than the other suitor nations with similar ambitions, some tough decisions need to be made soon.

items.title: Live: ASX rises as SpaceX shares see $1 trillion wiped
items.description: The Aussie share market opens up as SpaceX shares see more than $1 trillion wiped. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Why Australians shouldn't panic about fuel prices as war in Iran escalates again
items.description: With the price of oil rising and the fuel excise cut due to end, drivers are facing twin threats when it comes to the price of fuel, but experts say Australia is in a much better position compared with when the Middle East conflict began.

items.title: Iran frees US citizen after almost two years of imprisonment
items.description: Iran has freed a US-Iranian citizen detained since December, 2024 in what Trump says was a 'gesture of goodwill'.

items.title: Accused gangster to call on AFP in controversial deportation case
items.description: Lawyers for accused underworld figure Masood Zakaria want to call AFP Commissioner Krissy Barrett to give evidence as he seeks to have his murder charges thrown out of court.

items.title: Live: PM defends decision not to attend Garma Festival
items.description: Anthony Albanese defends his decision to break a promise and not to attend the Garma Festival this year. Follow live.

items.title: 'My father was an antisemite': Uni leader's personal submission to royal commission
items.description: The chancellor of Western Sydney University says tertiary institutions have hidden behind freedom of expression to avoid taking action on hate speech.

items.title: Images released to identify victims in alleged Sydney child abuser probe
items.description: Images of distinctive clothing have been released as authorities attempt to identify victims of a Sydney childcare worker who allegedly abused more than 130 children.

items.title: Liberal HQ says young voters don't remember Howard in 'reality check' to base
items.description: Liberal Party HQ has admitted it is "in the political fight of our lives" as it canvasses ideas, including reviving gender quotas, to take the party forward.

items.title: Country footballer handed life ban after opposition complaint
items.description: A player and assistant coach for a southern NSW AFL team has been handed a "life ban" following a tribunal hearing into eight offences.

items.title: Too many cooks spoil The Odyssey's bubbling epic
items.description: The scope of Christopher Nolan's latest epic might be awesome but a menagerie of supporting faces and questionable characterisations muddle the director's vision.

items.title: I thought I could use voodoo to win a TV competition, instead I won back my joy
items.description: Halfway through the Race Around The World competition, I'm second last on the leaderboard. So, I decide to cheat.

items.title: From Mozart to the Beatles, prove you're a music genius with this quiz
items.description: From famous icons and musical terms to unusual instruments and classical influences in popular music, test your knowledge with this quiz.

items.title: Decisions made by 'faceless people' in NDIS abandoning those in need, family says
items.description: Experts say the National Disability Insurance Scheme is failing people like Lucy, whose one-on-one care for severe disability has been deemed "not value for money".

items.title: The story behind Messi's photo with a future Spanish superstar
items.description: On Monday morning, Argentinian legend Lionel Messi will go up against rising Spanish superstar Lamine Yamal in the World Cup final, 19 years after their famous photo shoot.

items.title: Scars of alleged Invasion Day terror attack run deep six months on
items.description: A day of evidence reflecting on racism, hate and violence directed towards Aboriginal people highlights the ongoing impact of what police described as a potential "mass-casualty event" at a Perth rally.

items.title: Telstra and telco regulator prepare for grilling over widespread outage
items.description: Telstra prepares for a grilling in parliament about the recent network outage that disrupted Australia, with the communications regulator also set to face tough questions.

items.title: Artists seek ‘seat at table’ in AI office
items.description: The creative sector hopes there is a space to contribute to the Office of AI, given its content powers a lot of these tools.

items.title: Train drivers trapped, homes evacuated as wildfires rage across Canada's Ontario
items.description: Train operators in rural Canada were trapped by raging wildfires, as nearby communities were evacuated.

items.title: UK's Reform proposes round-the-clock protection for MPs
items.description: Britain's populist Reform UK, led by Nigel Farage, has called for all lawmakers to be given "full security" if they want it after the alleged murder of Ann Widdecombe, a prominent member of the party.

items.title: 'I want the money that is owed to me': Charity fails to pay $150k in super
items.description: Former staff of charity PAWS Darwin are speaking out about being short-changed on their superannuation to the tune of $150,000. Under-18 staff also say the super accounts PAWS promised to create for them never existed.
